inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition at 2026-06-30 (H1 2026 note 13.2): borrowings 11,113 less cash 4,951 and other current financial assets 313. inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY2025 continuing, unlevered and after leases: company 'Free cash flow' 3,006 + 128 Italy drag = 3,134 ex-Italy, less payments related to leases (principal + interest, net of subleases) 1,177 (lease treatment B), less SBC 18 = 1,939. This actual includes EUR 640m of property disposal proceeds and +EUR 263m of working capital / consumer-credit inflow that the forward build does NOT carry at those levels: the component build's normalised FY0 owner FCF is ~EUR 1,480m (EBITDA 3,330 - D&A ex-ROU 1,409 = EBIT 1,921, ties to ROI 2,158 + ROU depreciation 939 - lease payments 1,177; x (1-30%) + D&A - capex 1,523 + 0.25% recurring disposal credit). inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payments' 18 (FY2024 38, FY2023 53); H1 2026 12. The EUR 700-750m/yr programme of 2021-2024 was suspended for the Atacadao minority buyout; FY2025 saw a EUR 60m tax on the 2024 cancellations only. inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:38:09Z Euronext Paris regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the flows. BASE WACC 7.5%: risk-free 3.5% (10y OAT, Oct 2026, French political spread included), ERP 5.5%, equity beta 1.1 (grocery ~0.8 raw, lifted for leverage) -> cost of equity 9.55%; pre-tax cost of debt 3.7% (BBB EUR bonds, 2025 Atacadao refinancing), 2.6% after tax; D/(D+E) ~30% on EUR 9.8bn market cap and ~EUR 4.5bn average net debt -> 7.5%. EXPLICIT STRUCTURAL PREMIUMS added 2026-10-26 after the sanity check tripped (Step 8c.5 item 2), each documented against the house template: (a) concentrated geographic / currency risk +0.50%: ~30% of sales in Brazil and Argentina, BRL translation and IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting, Brazilian deferred-tax assets unrecognised (template band 0.5-1.5%, low end because France/Spain are the majority); (b) French regulatory / political exposure +0.50%: EGAlim-type retailer-supplier margin legislation, the 41.2% large-company surtax (FY2025 ETR 71%, H1 2026 55%), ADLC store-divestiture remedies on Cora/Match, and the October 2026 unrest that drove the guidance cut (template 'regulatory single point of failure' band 1.0-2.0%, applied at half because no single licence or regulator can stop the business); (c) thin-margin operating leverage / cyclicality +0.50%: reported operating income has ranged 758 (FY2018) to 2,463 (FY2022), >3x peak-to-trough, with sub-1% net margins so small operating misses are large equity misses (template band 1.0-2.0%, applied at half because recurring operating income is far steadier, 1,905-2,377). TOTAL WACC 9.0% in all three scenarios; France/LatAm downside is still charged in the bear flows and the 30% bear weight, but the premiums now also price the structural part of that risk in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full lease cash (principal + interest, net of sublease receipts: EUR 1,177m FY2025, 1,104 FY2024, up 3% H1 2026 on sale-and-leasebacks) is deducted inside the EBITDA margin path, so ebitda_margin_path is a pre-IFRS-16 margin: post-IFRS-16 EBITDA 4,507 (ROI 2,158 + D&A 2,349) less 1,177 = 3,330 = 3.96% of FY2025 revenue. Lease liabilities (EUR 4,971m) are excluded from net_debt. da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation: 1,345 owned P&E/intangibles + 64 supply chain = 1,409 (1.68%); ROU depreciation 721 + 218 = 939 is left out so the lease is not charged twice. Sanity multiples must therefore use ex-lease EV against post-lease EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; non-controlling interests (EUR 745m book at 2026-06-30, EUR 24m H1 2026 net income share, mainly Argentina/Belgium franchise partners after the 2025 Atacadao buyout took Brazil to 100%) are deducted once, at book, in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping toward the 2028/2030 'Carrefour 2030' targets in year 5). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer' with the adaptations file applied (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI at book, matching-asset rule for associates, SBC-light). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. SANITY FIX 2026-10-26: see valuation_philosophy.sanity_fix and sanity_check.fix_applied -- WACC 7.5% -> 9.0% with explicit premiums, base growth capped at the 0.72% through-cycle revenue CAGR from year 2, terminal caps reset to a no-re-rate basis (bear 8x / base 10x / bull 12x owner FCF). EBITDA MARGIN PATH (unchanged by the fix) absorbs ~0.3% of revenue of recurring 'non-recurring' cash charges (restructuring, store closures, GEPP plan: H1 2026 non-recurring expense EUR 165m) which sit below recurring operating income but inside the company's own net free cash flow; FY2025 pre-lease EBITDA 3.96% less ~0.3% = ~3.65% owner EBITDA base, base-year-1 3.60% after the riot hit. CAPEX PATH (unchanged) is net of a 0.25%-of-revenue recurring property-disposal credit (FY2024 595, FY2025 640 realised, ~0.75%; credited at one-third because the sale-and-leaseback pipeline is finite and each sale raises the lease charge). Gross capex guided EUR 1.6bn FY2026 (1.97% of pro-forma revenue), cut from 1.7bn on 2026-10-20. WORKING CAPITAL: structurally negative (suppliers 13.2-14.7bn vs inventories 6.7bn + receivables 3.3bn, ~-5% of revenue) so growth releases cash; 5% capture in base/bull, 0 in bear (consumer-credit book swings of +/-EUR 200m/yr are treated as noise); with growth capped at 0.72% this release is now immaterial in the base. CASH TAX: 32% in 2026 (French large-company surtax, Brazil deferred-tax assets not recognised; FY2025 cash tax 603 on pre-IFRS-16 EBIT 1,921 = 31%), 30% thereafter. FY2026 GUIDANCE (cut 2026-10-20): operating margin +0 to +15bp (was +25bp), adjusted EPS stable to slight growth (was high single digit), net FCF slight decline vs EUR 1,565m 2025 pro forma (was slight growth), capex EUR 1.6bn (was 1.7bn), on an EUR 80-200m operating-income hit from French riots, looting of ~50 stores, curfews and lost Q4 footfall. Base year-1 revenue +1.5% (H1 +2.0% reported, Q3 LFL +2.3%, Q4 impaired) and the owner EBITDA margin held ~flat-to-down. The component-built year-1 owner FCF (~EUR 1.1bn unlevered) sits well below the company's own guided NFCF of ~EUR 1.45-1.5bn plus ~EUR 280m finance costs, because the build credits only a third of the disposal proceeds and a fraction of the WC inflow; the gap is deliberate conservatism, not a forecast of underperformance. SEASONALITY: the equity bridge adds back EUR 1,900m of the June working-capital trough (observed seasonal swing 2.2-2.4bn, less the ~EUR 190m of H1 2026 underlying FCF that the year-1 projection already contains). Omitting it would deduct a cash outflow that reverses every December. Re-examined in the sanity fix and RETAINED: the H1 outflow is inside the June net debt and its H2 reversal is in neither the balance sheet nor the full-year flows (which assume WC neutral over a year), so the add-back is a consistency correction, not a valuation uplift; using the Dec-2025 balance sheet (3,965) with no add-back gives the same answer within EUR 16m. BAND POSITION: SBC is 0.02% of revenue, so house and street IV coincide; the engine's band_position is numerically meaningless and should be read as collapsed/n-a.
inputs.no_rerate_memo: Carrefour has traded at ~7-12x ex-lease EV / post-lease owner FCF for a decade and ~5-6x post-IFRS-16 EV/EBITDA. Today: market cap ~9.8bn + December-basis net debt ~3.95bn + NCI 0.75bn - associates 0.97bn = ~13.5bn ex-lease EV, which is ~9x the normalised FY2025 owner FCF of ~1,480m and ~7x the actual 1,939m. After the sanity fix the base terminal cap is 10x (no re-rating: the decade's typical multiple), bull 12x (the top of the decade range), bear 8x (the trough end). The prior build's 12x base cap assumed a one-third re-rating the market has refused for ten years; the required_return_table shows what return the current price implies at the base flows.

equity_bridge.item: Seasonal working-capital reversal (June net debt to December basis)
equity_bridge.note: H1 2025 WC -1,942 / FY2025 +475 and H1 2026 WC+consumer credit -2,173: December net debt is ~EUR 2.2-2.4bn below June every year. Added back less the ~EUR 190m of H1 2026 underlying FCF already in the FY2026 projection. Dec-2025 net debt was 3,965; 5,849 - 1,900 = 3,949 is the December-equivalent anchor. Retained through the 2026-10-26 sanity fix: it is a timing-consistency item (the H2 reversal is in neither the June balance sheet nor the full-year flows), equivalent to anchoring on the December balance sheet.
H1 2026 balance sheet, 2026-06-30; flows are 100% consolidated so NCI is charged here, once.

H1 2026 note 9.1: Carmila 30.0% (497), Provencia (137), Market Pay 35%, Showroomprive, CarrefourSA Turkey 32% (being sold for nominal consideration). Their income (EUR 14m H1, EUR 52m dividends received) is outside recurring operating income and therefore outside the flows, so the asset belongs in the bridge (matching-asset rule). Book, not market.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle revenue CAGR, FY2016 78,774 -> FY2025 84,025 over 9 years = 0.717%, applied at 0.7% so the capped path sits just under the cap rather than rounding above it (Step 8c.5 item 3: first-to-last year of available data, not the cyclical-recovery window). Adopted 2026-10-26 in place of the prior 2.0% judgment. The 5y revenue CAGR (3.1%, FY2020-25) is inflated by Argentine hyperinflation accounting and the Cora/Match and Casino-store scope additions and deflated by the Italy exit; the equity CAGR (2.3%) is depressed by EUR 2.9bn of 2021-24 buybacks and the FY2025 Italy loss; EPS CAGRs are negative on Italy, impairments and a 71% FY2025 ETR. The decade record is the honest anchor: Carrefour has grown ~0.7% nominal, i.e. shrunk in real terms, as it exited China, Taiwan, Italy and Romania and lost French share to E.Leclerc and discounters. Continuing LFL (+2.1-2.3% in 2026) is the bull-case rate, not the base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 2.3% vs revenue 3.1% vs EPS -9.9%: EPS diverges by far more than 30% (reported net income FY2025 EUR 319m on EUR 84bn revenue after Italy disposal losses, non-recurring charges and a 71% effective tax rate). Reported EPS is not a usable growth anchor for this name; FCF and ROI are. The same trough EPS (SBC-adjusted ~EUR 0.44) is the denominator of the sanity check's P/E rule, which is why that rule cannot be passed by any value above the current share price (the current share price alone is ~31.5x that EPS, already above 2x the 10yr average).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner series (Metrics.csv FCF less SBC): FY2020 1,881 -> FY2022 2,315 -> FY2025 2,407. SBC is ~0.02-0.06% of revenue throughout, so adjusted and reported CAGRs are within 0.1pp; SBC is not absorbing growth here. These CSV FCFs are BEFORE lease cash (EUR 1.0-1.2bn/yr), which the forward build deducts; the post-lease owner FCF level is roughly half the CSV figure in every year.

base.growth_rates_note: Year 1 +1.5% is half reported (H1 2026 +2.0%, Q3 LFL +2.3%, Q4 riot-impaired); years 2-10 held at 0.7%, just under the 0.717% through-cycle revenue CAGR, per Step 8c.5 item 3 (prior build: 2.0-2.5%; first pass used 0.72, which rounded above the cap). Terminal growth 1.0% for Gordon consistency with the capped path; the 10x cap binds in any case.
base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +1.5% (H1 +2.0%, Q3 LFL +2.3%, Q4 riot-impaired) with the owner EBITDA margin ~flat-to-down at 3.60% as the EUR 80-200m unrest hit and rising sale-and-leaseback rents offset the EUR 1bn cost programme; then nominal growth held at 0.7%, the decade's through-cycle rate (continuing LFL of ~2% offset by the pattern of portfolio exits, French share loss and BRL/ARS translation that has kept reported revenue flat for ten years) and ~45bp of pre-lease margin recovery to 4.10% by 2032, roughly half of management's 2030 target (ROI 3.5% vs 2.6% today). Gross capex 1.95% falling to 1.8% of revenue, with a third of the historical disposal credit; cash tax 32% then 30%; 5% working-capital capture on growth (now immaterial). Discounted at 9.0% (7.5% base WACC plus 1.5% of explicit structural premiums). Terminal 10x owner FCF = no re-rating from the decade's typical multiple (Gordon at 9%/1% would be ~12.6x; the cap binds).

bull.growth_rates_note: Bull growth trimmed from 3.0-3.5% to the continuing-LFL run-rate of 2.0% (year 1 2.5%): the bull case is now 'Carrefour keeps its current like-for-like without further portfolio shrinkage', not an acceleration. Terminal cap 12x = top of the decade's owner-FCF multiple range (Step 8c.5 item 4, bull = 10yr max).
bull.narrative: Unrest subsides by year-end and Q4 footfall normalises; the simplified three-market portfolio (France, Spain, Brazil) delivers the Carrefour 2030 plan: ROI margin 3.2% in 2028 and 3.5% in 2030, i.e. pre-lease owner EBITDA 4.6% by 2032, on EUR 1bn/yr cost savings, Cora/Match synergies (EUR 130m), own-brand at 40%, retail media (Unlimitail) and Atacadao store growth to 470+. Revenue holds the ~2% continuing like-for-like rate with no further exits. French surtax lapses and Brazilian deferred-tax assets are recognised (cash tax to 28%). Discounted at 9.0%. Terminal 12x: the market pays the top of the range it has paid Carrefour this decade, not an Ahold/Tesco multiple.

bear.growth_rates_note: Bear held below the 0.72% through-cycle cap (0% for two years, then 0.5%); prior build had 1.0-1.5% in later years, above the cap. Terminal cap 8x = trough end of the decade's owner-FCF multiple range (Step 8c.5 item 4, bear = 10yr min; today's ex-lease EV is ~7x actual FY2025 owner FCF).
bear.narrative: French unrest and curfews run into 2027 and the hit lands at the top of the EUR 80-200m range; E.Leclerc and Lidl keep taking share and Carrefour answers with price investment, so France hypermarket margins compress rather than recover; Poland deflation persists, BRL weakens and Argentina normalises away the IAS 29 nominal growth. Revenue flat through 2027 and ~0.5% thereafter; pre-lease owner EBITDA falls 85bp to 3.10% (France ROI margin squeeze) while rents keep indexing; the sale-and-leaseback pipeline is exhausted (no disposal credit, net capex 1.85%); the French surtax becomes permanent (32% cash tax); no working-capital release. 'Non-recurring' restructuring cash stays at 0.3%+ of revenue every year. The dividend is held but funded by the balance sheet, leverage stays near the June level, and the market de-rates the stock to ~8x owner FCF.

scenario_narratives.base: A structurally low-margin but cash-generative grocer that executes about half of its own 2030 margin plan while absorbing the 2026 French unrest as a one-year hit, on revenue that grows only at its decade-long 0.7% nominal rate. Axes: French market-share trajectory vs E.Leclerc/Lidl, sale-and-leaseback rent creep vs cost savings, Brazilian cash-and-carry growth vs BRL translation, and whether 'non-recurring' restructuring cash ever stops recurring.
scenario_narratives.bull: Portfolio simplification and the cost programme deliver the Carrefour 2030 targets; revenue holds its ~2% like-for-like with no further exits; the stock re-rates to the top of its own decade range (~12x owner FCF) as net FCF grows per the EUR 5bn 2026-28 cumulative target.
scenario_narratives.bear: France deteriorates structurally (security situation plus price war), margins compress toward 3.1% pre-lease, revenue stalls, the stock de-rates to ~8x owner FCF, and the company remains a high-FCF-yield value trap funding dividends while equity value stagnates.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 30%: the guidance cut is days old and management itself calls the French situation 'deep uncertainty' into the peak quarter; net margins are sub-1% so small operating misses are large equity misses; net debt is at a seasonal high with S&P BBB; and Carrefour has a decade-long record of missing medium-term margin targets. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: unrest subsiding, France share stabilising, the 3.5% 2030 margin target, Brazilian macro and a multiple re-rating the market has refused for ten years. Base 50%. Weights unchanged by the 2026-10-26 sanity fix: the fix moved the rate, the growth path and the terminal caps, and the structural risk is now priced partly in the WACC premiums, but the bear probability is about the next 12-24 months in France and nothing in the sanity check bears on it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Carrefour on unlevered owner FCF after all lease cash and after the recurring restructuring charges the company books below recurring operating income, discounted at a EUR WACC that carries explicit premiums for its LatAm currency exposure, French regulatory/political risk and thin-margin operating leverage, with revenue growth held at the decade's 0.72% through-cycle rate and terminal value capped at the owner-FCF multiples the market has actually paid Carrefour (8x/10x/12x). The June 2026 balance sheet is the anchor with an explicit, documented seasonal working-capital add-back rather than a stale December figure. The component build is deliberately below the company's own net-FCF framing (disposal proceeds credited at a third, working capital at a fraction). After the sanity fix the base case assumes NO re-rating, so any upside the model shows is the gap between the owner-FCF yield at today's price and a 9% required return, not a multiple expansion story. The required-return table is the key output: it says what IRR the current price implies on base flows for a thin-margin French retailer with LatAm currency exposure.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_fix: WHAT TRIPPED (sanity_check.py 2026-10-25, exit 3): implied P/E 56.9x on the base case vs 2x the 10yr average of 15.5x. P/B 1.56x and P/Sales 0.204x did not formally trip but both sat ABOVE the decade's maximum (1.31x and 0.180x): the base case was pricing a re-rating the market has not granted in ten years. CAUSE: not peak-earnings extrapolation (the owner-FCF base of ~EUR 1.48bn normalised is already below FY2025 actual 1.94bn and below guidance), so Step 8c.5 item 1 was not applied. The P/E rule divides by FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS of ~EUR 0.44, a trough year (net income EUR 319m after the Italy disposal loss and a 71% effective tax rate, vs 1,659m in FY2023); the current share price alone is 31.5x that denominator, so no value above the market price can pass the 31x threshold, and the number should be read against adjusted EPS (~9x at the current price) instead. The fixable causes were (i) growth of 2.0-2.5% against a 0.72% through-cycle revenue CAGR and (ii) a 7.5% WACC that did not price structural risks the qualitative analysis names. WHAT CHANGED (Step 8c.5 items 2-4, one pass): WACC 7.5% -> 9.0% in all scenarios via three documented premiums (+0.5% LatAm geographic/currency, +0.5% French regulatory/political, +0.5% thin-margin cyclicality; see inputs.wacc_rationale); base revenue growth capped at the through-cycle CAGR (0.717%, applied at 0.7%) from year 2 (year 1 held at the half-reported +1.5%), bull trimmed to the 2.0% continuing-LFL rate, bear held at 0-0.5%; terminal caps reset on a no-re-rate basis to bear 8x / base 10x / bull 12x owner FCF (EV/EBITDA history is null for this ticker, so the decade's observed owner-FCF multiple range is used as the binding cap, with the engine printing the implied terminal EV/EBITDA for cross-check); base terminal growth 2.0% -> 1.0% for consistency with the capped path (non-binding, the cap binds). UNCHANGED, deliberately: margin, D&A, capex and cash-tax paths (evidence-based and not named by the diagnosis), the 30/50/20 weights, and the EUR 1,900m seasonal working-capital add-back, which was re-examined and retained because it is a timing-consistency item equivalent to anchoring on the December balance sheet, not an uplift. RESULT: see sanity_check.implied_multiples_after_fix. The P/E rule remains formally tripped because of its trough-EPS denominator; P/B and P/Sales move from above the decade maximum to inside the decade range, which is the test that carries information for this name. No further iteration: a value low enough to pass the P/E rule would have to sit below the share price, which is not a defensible modelling target.
key_risks_to_valuation: French social unrest extends beyond Q4 2026 or recurs; the EUR 80-200m hit becomes a run-rate cost (security, insurance, closures) and Q4 footfall does not return
Continued French share loss to E.Leclerc and discounters forces price investment, so the pre-lease margin falls rather than recovers (bear path)
Sale-and-leaseback and rent indexation raise lease cash faster than cost savings; management's post-IFRS-16 ROI margin targets then overstate owner economics
BRL/ARS depreciation and the end of Argentine hyperinflation accounting shrink reported nominal growth; Brazil deferred-tax assets stay unrecognised
'Non-recurring' restructuring cash charges (Cora GEPP, store closures, Spain/Argentina) persist above the 0.3% of revenue assumed
The seasonal working-capital add-back (EUR 1,900m, ~EUR 2.7/share) assumes December payables normalise; a weak Q4 would unwind part of it
Growth cap: the 0.72% through-cycle rate embeds a decade of deliberate exits; if the three-market portfolio actually compounds at its ~2% LFL the base understates value (that is the bull case)
WACC premiums are judgment: each 0.5% of the 1.5% added moves the base value by roughly EUR 1/share
Terminal multiple: the base assumes 10x owner FCF, i.e. no re-rating; the dashboard's sensitivity shows the value if the market pays 12x (bull) or de-rates to 8x (bear)
Equity-accounted stakes (Carmila etc.) carried at EUR 967m book; CarrefourSA Turkey is being sold for nominal consideration

sanity_check.fix_applied: 2026-10-26, one pass per Step 8c.5. Trip: implied P/E 56.9x on base IV 24.96 vs 2x 10yr avg 15.5x; P/B 1.56x and P/Sales 0.204x were also above the decade maxima (1.31x, 0.180x). Not a peak-earnings case (item 1 skipped: owner-FCF base already normalised below actual and below guidance). Applied item 2: WACC 7.5% -> 9.0% with explicit premiums (+0.5% LatAm geographic/currency, +0.5% French regulatory/political, +0.5% thin-margin cyclicality), documented in inputs.wacc_rationale. Applied item 3: base revenue growth capped at the through-cycle CAGR (FY2016-FY2025 = 0.717%, applied at 0.7%) from year 2, bull trimmed to 2.0% continuing LFL, bear 0-0.5%; selected_growth_rate 2.0 -> 0.7. Second (final) adjustment after the first pass still tripped: capped years trimmed 0.72 -> 0.70 so the growth_too_high candidate clears exactly; a further WACC increase was NOT taken because passing the P/E rule would require a base value below the share price. Applied item 4: terminal caps reset to the decade's observed owner-FCF multiple range, bear 8x / base 10x / bull 12x (EV/EBITDA history null; engine prints implied terminal EV/EBITDA for cross-check). Unchanged: margin/D&A/capex/tax paths, 30/50/20 weights, EUR 1,900m seasonal WC add-back (re-examined, retained as a timing-consistency item). The P/E rule divides by trough FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS (~EUR 0.44; 71% ETR, Italy disposal loss) and is already at 31.5x on the current share price, so it cannot be passed by any value above the market price; it is reported as still tripped rather than engineered around.

implied_multiples_after_fix.verdict: P/B and P/Sales moved from above the 10yr maximum to the 10yr average (1.04x vs 1.06x avg; 0.136x vs 0.141x avg). P/E 38.0x remains above the 31x threshold (2x the 15.5x average) because the rule divides by trough FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS of ~EUR 0.44 (net income EUR 319m after the Italy disposal loss, 71% ETR); the current share price alone is 31.5x that denominator, so no value above the market price can pass it. Reported as still tripped; not engineered around. Bridge prior weighted 21.88 -> 14.98: WACC 7.5->9.0% approx -3.5, base/bull/bear growth caps approx -1.6, terminal caps 12/14/10 -> 10/12/8 approx -1.8 (interactions included).
